title: add performance canary pipeline, automated regression detection, and rollout guards
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: This PR introduces a production-facing performance canary pipeline that continuously runs representative inference workloads, detects latency/throughput regressions automatically, and wires automated rollout guards into the deployment flow. Motivation: recent incidents highlighted a gap between CI perf checks and real-world serving patterns (KV cache behavior and tail latencies). We want early detection of regressions that affect SLOs before automatic rollouts. What this PR does: 1) Adds a new perf-canary service under infra/perf-canary that schedules synthetic traffic (mix of chat/text-gen/embedding/rerank) against canary model variants and records percentile latencies, throughput, and token-level cost metrics. 2) Implements automated anomaly detection rules (baseline windows + thresholds + nonparametric tests) that surface regressions for P50/P95/P99 latency and effective throughput; alerts are pushed to PagerDuty and Slack and create Linear issues when thresholds are breached. 3) Integrates canary results into the rollout controller: a new RolloutGuard CRD-compatible signal that blocks automatic canary->stable promotion when perf regressions exceed configured tolerances; supports manual override with audit log. 4) Adds e2e perf tests and a local-mode simulator to run the canary harness in dev and CI. 5) Adds observability dashboards (Grafana) and a lightweight exporter for canary metrics to the existing telemetry pipeline. 6) Documentation: quickstart, config reference, and runbook for investigating canaries. Implementation notes: - The canary harness uses the same request path and batching profile as production to preserve realistic batching/KV cache behavior; we replay representative prompts based on sampled prod prompt histograms. - Regression detection uses a rolling baseline (2d window) + median-of-differences bootstrapped confidence intervals to reduce sensitivity to skewed traffic. - RolloutGuard hooks into the existing rollout controller; we added a conservative default tolerance (P95 +15% and P99 +10% cost impact) and make it configurable per-release via rollout_policy. - To minimize noise, we added auto-throttling to the harness and a calibration step that aligns the canary load with the target GPU pool saturation. Backwards compatibility and safety: the changes are opt-in via cluster-level feature flag perf_canaries.enabled=false by default for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers will be opted-in by default with admin control. The change does not alter runtime serving codepaths except small telemetry hooks; those are feature-flagged and tested. Migration and rollout: - Initial rollout will run canaries for model rollouts longer (24h) for the first two weeks and surface results in the Redwood Console rollout page. - Ops playbook added to infra/runbooks/perf-canary-runbook.md. Security/Privacy: requests in the harness are sampled and tokenized; no customer data is used for canaries. Related work: follows design notes in ENG-2154 and complements perf-canary PoC from ENG-1987. Caveats: anomaly detector tuned conservatively for now; further tuning expected after 1-2 weeks of signals. Test plan: unit tests for detection logic, integration tests for harness replay, CI e2e job (runs in low-load mode), and manual canary runs on staging.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can you elaborate on how the baseline window is chosen? I worry about seasonality causing false positives.
Priya Shah (author): Baseline is 48h by default; we've added a dynamic fallback that expands to 72h when variance is high. Added notes in detector.py and docs.
Maya Rodriguez (reviewer): The RolloutGuard API looks good; please ensure the audit log includes which metric tripped the guard.
Priya Shah (author): Added explicit audit fields: metric_name, baseline_pct_change, detected_at. See rollout_guard.go lines ~120.
Ethan Park (reviewer): CI perf job runtime is long — can we gate full runs behind a nightly job?
Priya Shah (author): CI will run a short smoke e2e (<10m) on PRs; full harness runs are scheduled nightly. Updated ci/jobs/perf-canary.yml accordingly.
Maya Rodriguez (approver): Approved after addressing audit log and CI gating comments.
Liam O'Connor (approver): LGTM. Verified canary metrics in staging and RolloutGuard prevented a simulated P95 regression.
An automated review (CI): flake8 failed on infra/perf-canary/harness.py; fixed in c3b1f8d -> 9a6e2b5 follow-up commit.
release_notes: Adds continuous performance canary pipeline, automated regression detection for latency/throughput, RolloutGuard integration to block problematic rollouts, Grafana dashboards, and runbook. Feature-flagged and opt-in for Dedicated/Private.
